children: Comstock Resources has lined up a $1.65 billion investment from Azerbaijan's state oil company to help cut debt and fund the development of its Haynesville shale assets.

The company has signed a letter of intent with State Oil Company of the Azerbaijan Republic, or SOCAR, for the sale of 20% of Comstock's interest in the Legacy Haynesville upstream assets, as well as 15% of Comstock's interest in its Western Haynesville upstream assets. The Western Haynesville stake will reduce to 7.5% after five years once SOCAR achieves a 15% return on investment in those assets.
SOCAR will also buy 15% of Comstock's 73% ownership interest in Pinnacle Gas Services, a subsidiary that provides midstream services to the Western Haynesville.

The letter of intent binds the companies to negotiate a definitive agreement in good faith, which they aim to execute by the end of October. Closing the deal will be subject to conditions including any required government approvals.

Comstock, a natural gas producer focused on developing the Haynesville shale in North Louisiana and East Texas, said SOCAR will have the opportunity to participate in future opportunities in the Legacy and Western Haynesville at the same percentages the Azerbaijan-based company is acquiring in the transaction and SOCAR will provide opportunities for Comstock to market its gas to international customers.

Comstock said the $1.65 billion purchase price is a validation of the value of its asset base and introduces a reputable international partner that brings a large investment-grade balance sheet. The funding will be used to reduce Comstock's total debt to roughly $1.5 billion from $3.1 billion as of the end of June

With a strengthened balance sheet, Comstock plans to continue work on its 545,000 net acres in the Western Haynesville, one of the largest undeveloped natural gas resources in the U.S. The company will remain operator of all its upstream assets and will continue to manage, operate and control Pinnacle Gas Services.

Comstock said it additionally entered into a Haynesville shale drilling venture with Jerry Jones, the company's majority stockholder. Beginning Sept. 1, a partnership owned by the Jones family will fund the drilling and completion costs of 85% of 18 Western Haynesville wells and 80% of nine Legacy Haynesville wells being drilled and completed by Comstock over the next 12 months, which is expected to cost about $450 million. After a 15% return on investment is achieved, half of the interest in the wells will revert to Comstock.
